de31_watchdogs.topic: Inspectors general removed 2025; Storch v. Hegseth; precedent 2009/2020/2022/2024

claims.text: About 17 inspectors general were dismissed by email effective immediately on the night of Friday 24 January 2025; Congress did not receive the 30-day notice; Grassley: 'the 30 day detailed notice of removal that the law demands was not provided to Congress' and 'There may be good reason the IGs were fired. We need to know that if so.'; Warren: 'a purge of independent watchdogs in the middle of the night'

Judge Ana Reyes, 24 September 2025: 'President Trump violated the IGA. That much is obvious'; denied injunction restoring the eight plaintiff IGs (no irreparable harm; the president could re-fire after proper notice); left back pay open pending Slaughter; 'deserved better from their government. They still do.'
DOJ attorney at March 2025 hearing: 'we don't dispute that the president did not comply with the sentence in the statute', arguing the law does not require prior notice

Storch v. Hegseth stayed 25 Sep 2025 pending Slaughter; joint status report 13 Jul 2026; 20 Jul 2026 minute order set pre-motion conference for summary judgment (requests due 3 Aug, conference week of 24 Aug 2026); no ruling on the merits shown on the docket as of late October 2026
Obama removed AmeriCorps/CNCS IG Gerald Walpin in June 2009, saying he had 'lost confidence'; Grassley questioned whether the 30-day notice requirement was met

December 2022 amendments (P.L. 117-263) require a 'substantive rationale, including detailed and case-specific reasons' for IG removal; first tests were Biden's notices for the Railroad Retirement Board IG (29 March 2024) and Commerce acting IG (1 May 2024); Grassley argued the RRB notice lacked detail; in 2020 Trump replaced several IGs including those at Defense and the intelligence community

de31_purse.topic: Spending control: GAO ICA findings, pocket rescission, Supreme Court stay; precedent Ukraine 2019 and Biden wall pause 2021

claims.text: GAO decision B-337204 (29 Sep 2025) found FEMA violated the ICA, 'The burden to justify withholdings rests with FEMA'; the Senate Appropriations minority listed it as GAO's seventh ICA violation finding of 2025: EV charging (May), museum and library (June), Head Start (July), K-12 energy efficiency (July), NIH (August), FEMA FY2025 and FEMA FY2021-24 (September)
GAO B-331564, 16 January 2020: 'OMB violated the ICA when it withheld USAI funds for a policy reason'; 'not a programmatic delay'
GAO, 15 June 2021: Biden's pause of more than $1 billion in border wall funds was a 'programmatic delay', not an impoundment; Shelby and Capito said it showed 'two sets of rules'

Pocket rescission special message 28 Aug 2025, nearly $5 billion in foreign aid expiring 30 Sep; OMB: Congress 'considered the possible effects of withholding funds close to the end of the fiscal year'; GAO B-330330.1: section 1012(b) 'may not lawfully be used to effect a pocket recission'; presidents of both parties have withheld funds proposed for rescission

Supreme Court, 26 Sep 2025, unsigned order: ICA likely precluded the recipients' suit; 'the asserted harms to the Executive's conduct of foreign affairs appear to outweigh the potential harm'; about $4bn of the $4.9bn; Kagan (with Sotomayor, Jackson): 'effectively altered the balance of power between Congress and the president over the power of the purse'; Vought: 'major victory'
